gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-biorhyme-expanded: Happy Monkey draws every stroke like a marker line, bold and uniform, while BioRhyme Expanded spreads out below it in wide, bookish serif letters. Pages feel unhurried.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-biz-udmincho: Happy Monkey has a ruler-straight, marker-like stroke that looks bold and playful. Next to it, BIZ UDMincho feels like a traditional text serif with a shallow curl, so the two read as a joker and a scholar sharing a desk.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-copse: Straight, unvarying strokes mark Happy Monkey, with no hairlines and no swelling anywhere. Copse follows as a literary serif with daylight in every curve, which gives the loud heading a bookish neighbor.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-cutive: Distinctive is the word for Happy Monkey, whose marker-like line stays steady through every letter and makes headings hard to ignore. And Cutive, a refined text serif with wide tracking, does the opposite job, letting running text drift along gently.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-david-libre: Happy Monkey's strokes never pinch at the curves, which gives it a bold, blunt charm. David Libre adds dignity as a serif with open-hanging terminals, and that mix of swagger and refinement is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-enriqueta: Happy Monkey has no pinched joints and no flared ends, just bold, plain marker-style strokes from start to finish. Enriqueta, a literary text serif with chalky curves, carries the body text beneath it.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-fenix: Fenix reads like a classic serif with an editorial bent, its curved strokes ending before they turn inward and giving lines a polished feel. Happy Monkey's thick, unchanging lines make a strong opposite, loud where Fenix is formal.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gentium-plus: Gentium Plus reads as a refined serif, each c opening like the mouth of a pitcher. Happy Monkey, with its single monoline stroke, earns its place on big, short headings.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gowun-batang: Refined describes Gowun Batang, yet the boldness comes from Happy Monkey, whose crossbars match its stems in thickness. Gowun Batang, a classic serif with terminals cut back for a big gap, handles the quiet reading instead.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-habibi: Habibi reads like a traditional text serif, with a clear channel leading into each round letter. Over a long stretch it keeps a steady editorial rhythm, while Happy Monkey's heading has no thick and thin parts at all.
